title: The Fox and the Cat

full_text:
A proud fox met a humble grey cat in the forest and looked down upon her with haughty disdain. "Good day, mistress cat," sneered the fox. "How do you manage to survive in these dangerous times? How many clever arts and tricks do you possess?"

"I know only one single art," replied the cat modestly.

"Only one?" laughed the fox boastfully. "How pitiful! I am master of a hundred arts, and besides that, I possess a sack full of cunning tricks that can outwit any hunter or hound in the world!"

Just then, four ferocious hunting hounds came bounding through the thicket, barking fiercely, followed by hunters on swift horses.

In an instant, the cat used her one art: she sprang up the trunk of a tall birch tree and sat safely in the high branches, sheltered by the dense leaves. "Open your sack of tricks, master fox!" called the cat from above. "Use your hundred arts!"

The boastful fox darted this way and that, doubling back, leaping over ditches, and trying all hundred of his cunning tricks. But the hounds surrounded him, cut off his escape, and captured him in the briars.

Watching from her secure perch, the cat sighed: "Master Fox, all your hundred arts could not save your skin, while my single modest art has kept me safe and sound!"
moral: One reliable, practical skill is worth more than a hundred boastful tricks that fail in danger.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Fox and the Cat"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
